newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israeli defence chief says Hebron deal imminent.
newsitem.headline: Israeli defence chief says Hebron deal imminent.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Tuesday that a long-elusive Hebron deal with the Palestinians was imminent.
"I estimate the signing will take place soon, today, tomorrow or the day after," he told reporters after meeting President Hosni Mubarak in the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Hurghada.

The defence minister, speaking in Egypt before returning to Israel, said he had been briefed on talks on Tuesday between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat aimed at closing a deal.

In Jerusalem, a senior Israeli official briefing reporters said he believed a deal would be signed within a week. Israel Radio said the deal would be initialled very soon before being put to the Israeli cabinet for approval.

The Israeli-PLO summit on Hebron failed to wrap up a deal in time for Christmas Eve but U.S. envoy Dennis Ross reported "real progress" towards the long-elusive accord to give Arafat's Palestinian Authority control of 80 percent of Hebron.

Netanyahu has insisted on protection for the 400 Jews living and studying in the heart of 100,000 Arabs in Hebron, a hotbed of Moslem and Jewish militancy seized by Israel with the rest of the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East war.

Mordechai said he expected Netanyahu and Mubarak to meet after the Hebron signing. On at least two occasions in the past three months Mubarak, whose country signed a treaty with Israel in 1979, has refused to meet Netanyahu until Hebron is settled.

"I know the prime minister talks to the president and after the signing of the agreement on Hebron, there will be a meeting in Cairo or some place else in which relations between the two countries will be furthered," Mordechai said.

Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab state to make peace with Israel but relations have been tense since Netanyahu's election on a platform committed to Jewish settlement of occupied Arab lands and opposed to swapping occupied land for peace.
Mordechai emerged from a two-hour meeting with Mubarak holding hands with the Egyptian president.
Later the Iraqi-born defence minister told reporters: "We held hands more than once. We spoke in Arabic and in English. The body language, the eye contact, I found him to be a very engaging man."

He said he raised the issue of Egyptian-held Israeli Azam Azam and gave Mubarak his "word of honour" the prisoner held on suspicion of spying was not associated in any way with any Israeli intelligence agency.
